title: Watermark Basins: Black-Box Detection of Distilled LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.37266v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Proprietary language models and their reasoning traces are vulnerable to API-based distillation, where an adversary trains a student model on the teacher model's outputs. To obtain evidence of distillation, model providers can watermark the teacher's outputs, aiming to leave a radioactive signal in the student's outputs. Existing black-box detectors search for such radioactivity using token-level statistics of the suspect model's outputs. However, token-level signals are not always detectable, for instance when the distillation traces are sampled at a low temperature. In this work, we discover the watermark basin, a persistent signal that enables more reliable watermark detection: during fine-tuning, watermarked teacher traces embed a distinct, key-specific geometric signal in parameter space that lies orthogonal to the ordinary task-specific fine-tuning subspace. translated_title: 水印盆地：蒸馏大语言模型的黑盒检测
translated_abstract: 专有语言模型及其推理轨迹容易受到基于API的蒸馏攻击，即攻击者利用教师模型的输出来训练学生模型。为了获得蒸馏发生的证据，模型提供商可以对教师模型的输出进行水印处理，力求在学生模型的输出中留下“放射性”信号。现有的黑盒检测器通过分析可疑模型输出的token级统计信息来搜寻这种放射性信号。然而，token级信号并不总是可检测的，例如当蒸馏轨迹在低温采样条件下生成时。在这项工作中，我们发现了“水印盆地”——一种能够实现更可靠水印检测的持久性信号：在微调过程中，带水印的教师轨迹会在参数空间中嵌入一种独特的、与密钥相关的几何信号，该信号与普通的任务特定微调子空间正交。基于这一发现，我们提出了水印盆地对齐方法（WM-Basin）……（摘要截断）
tldr: 本文发现了“水印盆地”现象——带水印教师模型的蒸馏学生模型会在参数空间中留下与密钥相关且与任务微调子空间正交的持久几何信号，据此提出的WM-Basin黑盒检测方法比传统的token级统计检测在低温采样等困难场景下更加可靠。
en_tdlr: This paper discovers the "watermark basin"—a persistent, key-specific geometric signal embedded in the parameter space of student models distilled from watermarked teachers, lying orthogonal to task-specific fine-tuning subspaces—and introduces WM-Basin, a black-box detector that is more reliable than token-level statistical methods, even under low-temperature distillation.
